The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). 1	# Flow Evaluators Guide
2	
3	The seven evaluator types for `uip maestro flow eval evaluator add --type <type>`. Flow uses the same `uipath-*` evaluator type IDs as the coded evaluator engine (NOT the legacy IDs the low-code `uipath-agents` skill uses). Each `--type` kebab-case value maps to a `uipath-*` evaluator under the hood:
4	
5	| `--type` flag | Internal `evaluatorTypeId` | LLM-based | Score scale |
6	|---------------|---------------------------|-----------|-------------|
7	| `exact-match` | `uipath-exact-match` | No | Binary (0/1) |
8	| `json-similarity` | `uipath-json-similarity` | No | Continuous (0–1) |
9	| `contains` | `uipath-contains` | No | Binary (0/1) |
10	| `llm-judge-output` | `uipath-llm-judge-output-semantic-similarity` | Yes | Continuous (0–1) |
11	| `llm-judge-strict-json` | `uipath-llm-judge-output-strict-json-similarity` | Yes | Continuous (0–1) |
12	| `llm-judge-trajectory` | `uipath-llm-judge-trajectory-similarity` | Yes | Continuous (0–1) |
13	| `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | `uipath-llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | Yes | Continuous (0–1) |
14	
15	The four classification and tool-call evaluators (`uipath-binary-classification`, `uipath-multiclass-classification`, `uipath-tool-call-*`) that exist in the coded SDK are **not** exposed by `uip maestro flow eval evaluator add`. Use the seven listed above.
16	
17	## When to Pick Each Type
18	
19	| Goal | Type | Notes |
20	|------|------|-------|
21	| Strict equality of a known output value | `exact-match` | Binary; no LLM. Cheapest. Use for deterministic agents. |
22	| Compare structured JSON outputs with tolerance for ordering / minor diffs | `json-similarity` | Tree-based; numeric tolerance ~1%, string Levenshtein. |
23	| Pass/fail on whether a substring appears | `contains` | Use `--search-text` on the data point, not the evaluator. |
24	| Score natural-language similarity between expected and actual | `llm-judge-output` | Default LLM judge. Set `--model`. |
25	| Per-key strict JSON scoring with LLM judgment on differences | `llm-judge-strict-json` | LLM penalizes per-field. Use when each output key matters independently. |
26	| Score whether the agent's reasoning path matches expected behavior | `llm-judge-trajectory` | Reads agent run history. Use `--expected-agent-behavior` on data points. |
27	| As above but with simulated tool calls / inputs | `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | Use when the flow can't safely execute real tools during eval. |
28	
29	## Adding an Evaluator (CLI)
30	
31	```bash
32	# Deterministic — no model needed
33	uip maestro flow eval evaluator add exact-greeting \
34	  --type exact-match \
35	  --target-key "greeting" \
36	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
37	
38	# LLM-judge — model is effectively required
39	uip maestro flow eval evaluator add greeting-quality \
40	  --type llm-judge-output \
41	  --model gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 \
42	  --description "Score greeting tone and completeness" \
43	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
44	```
45	
46	Critical: pass `--model` on every `llm-judge-*` evaluator. Empty `model` triggers a 500 from the LLM gateway only after retries — unfriendly to debug.
47	
48	## `--target-key`
49	
50	Defaults to `*` (the entire output object). Set a specific key when only one field of the output should be scored:
51	
52	- Output: `{"greeting": "Hello!", "metadata": {"latencyMs": 12}}` 
53	- `--target-key "greeting"` scores only the greeting string, ignoring metadata noise.
54	- `--target-key "*"` (default) scores the whole object.
55	
56	## Evaluator JSON Shape
57	
58	The CLI writes evaluator JSON files into the project's evaluator directory. Filenames follow `<name>-<suffix>.json` for CLI-created files; hand-written files can use any descriptive name. Let `eval set add` write `evaluatorRefs` instead of hand-editing them.
59	
60	### Deterministic example (`exact-match`)
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "id": "<generate-uuid>",
65	  "name": "exact-greeting",
66	  "description": "Strict greeting match",
67	  "version": "1.0",
68	  "evaluatorTypeId": "uipath-exact-match",
69	  "evaluatorConfig": {
70	    "name": "exact-greeting",
71	    "targetOutputKey": "greeting",
72	    "caseSensitive": false,
73	    "negated": false
74	  }
75	}
76	```
77	
78	`exact-match`, `json-similarity`, and `contains` do NOT carry a `model` or `prompt`.
79	
80	### LLM-judge example (`llm-judge-output`)
81	
82	```json
83	{
84	  "id": "<generate-uuid>",
85	  "name": "greeting-quality",
86	  "description": "Score greeting tone and completeness",
87	  "version": "1.0",
88	  "evaluatorTypeId": "uipath-llm-judge-output-semantic-similarity",
89	  "evaluatorConfig": {
90	    "name": "greeting-quality",
91	    "model": "gpt-4.1-2025-04-14",
92	    "temperature": 0,
93	    "maxTokens": 4096,
94	    "targetOutputKey": "*",
95	    "prompt": "Score 0-1 the semantic similarity of {{ActualOutput}} vs {{ExpectedOutput}}. Return JSON {\"score\": N, \"reason\": \"...\"}."
96	  }
97	}
98	```
99	
100	Template variables per type:
101	
102	| Type | Placeholders |
103	|------|-------------|
104	| `llm-judge-output` | `{{ExpectedOutput}}`, `{{ActualOutput}}` |
105	| `llm-judge-strict-json` | `{{ExpectedOutput}}`, `{{ActualOutput}}` |
106	| `llm-judge-trajectory` | `{{AgentRunHistory}}`, `{{ExpectedAgentBehavior}}`, `{{UserOrSyntheticInput}}` |
107	| `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | `{{AgentRunHistory}}`, `{{ExpectedAgentBehavior}}`, `{{UserOrSyntheticInput}}`, `{{SimulationInstructions}}` |
108	
109	When `--prompt` is omitted, the CLI inserts a built-in default for each type. Override with `--prompt` only when you need different wording or scoring criteria — keep the same placeholders.
110	
111	## Custom Prompts
112	
113	```bash
114	uip maestro flow eval evaluator add strict-match \
115	  --type llm-judge-output \
116	  --model gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 \
117	  --prompt 'Score 0-1 how closely {{ActualOutput}} matches {{ExpectedOutput}}. Return JSON {"score": N, "reason": "..."}.' \
118	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
119	```
120	
121	Unknown placeholders are passed through to the LLM as literal text — they are not silent errors but they will not be substituted with run data.
122	
123	## Removing an Evaluator
124	
125	```bash
126	uip maestro flow eval evaluator remove greeting-quality \
127	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
128	```
129	
130	Removing an evaluator does NOT auto-clean `evaluatorRefs` arrays in eval sets that reference it. After removing, re-list eval sets and reconcile any stale refs:
131	
132	```bash
133	uip maestro flow eval set list --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
134	```
135	
136	## Anti-patterns
137	
138	- **Don't pass `--type` in PascalCase.** `ExactMatch` fails; only `exact-match` is accepted.
139	- **Don't omit `--model` on `llm-judge-*`.** The cloud worker fail-fasts before calling the LLM gateway; the resulting 500 is unhelpful.
140	- **Don't hand-write evaluator refs unless you are repairing an eval set.** Omit `--evaluators` so the CLI links all current evaluators, or use `eval set add --evaluators <generated_id_or_file_base>`. Do not pass the evaluator display name.
141	- **Don't copy evaluator JSON across projects without regenerating UUIDs.** `id` collisions silently corrupt resolution.
142	- **Don't use deterministic evaluators (`exact-match`, `json-similarity`, `contains`) for natural-language outputs.** They will fail almost every test that paraphrases.
143	- **Don't mix trajectory and output evaluators on the same data point unless the data point provides both `--expected` and `--expected-agent-behavior`.** Otherwise one of them scores against an empty placeholder.
144

1	# Eval Sets and Data Points
2	
3	An eval set is a JSON file that bundles test cases (data points) with the evaluators that score them. Each Flow project can have multiple eval sets — typically one per scenario (smoke, regression, edge cases).
4	
5	## Eval Set Lifecycle
6	
7	```bash
8	# Create
9	uip maestro flow eval set add "<set_name>" \
10	  [--evaluators <ref1>,<ref2>] \
11	  [--entry-point <node_id>] \
12	  --path <flow_project> --output json
13	
14	# List
15	uip maestro flow eval set list --path <flow_project> --output json
16	
17	# Remove
18	uip maestro flow eval set remove "<id_or_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
19	```
20	
21	### `--evaluators`
22	
23	Comma-separated list of evaluator IDs or generated file base names. When omitted, the new eval set links to **all evaluators** present in the project at creation time and writes the generated evaluator file refs (for example, `greeting-match-62c0793a.json`). Prefer omission when the eval set should use every current evaluator.
24	
25	Do **not** pass an evaluator display name such as `greeting-match` to `--evaluators`; that writes the display name into `evaluatorRefs`, and Studio Web eval runs will not resolve it. If you need an explicit list, get the generated id/file ref from `uip maestro flow eval evaluator add/list --output json` and pass that value instead.
26	
27	Subsequent evaluators added to the project do NOT auto-attach — link them by re-running `set add` with explicit generated refs, or carefully repair the eval set's `evaluatorRefs` array using the evaluator file refs the CLI created.
28	
29	### `--entry-point`
30	
31	Stored as `selectedEntrypoint` on the eval set. Accepts either:
32	
33	- A flow path: `/Main.bpmn#start`
34	- A start node ID: `start_a1b2c3d4`
35	
36	The eval set's entry point is used by `eval run start` unless `--entry-point` is overridden at run time. Pin one explicitly when the flow has multiple entry points; otherwise the first start node found is used and may not be the one you intend.
37	
38	## Data Point Lifecycle
39	
40	Data points (test cases) live **inline** inside the eval set JSON, not as separate files. CRUD via `uip maestro flow eval add/list/remove`:
41	
42	```bash
43	# Add a data point
44	uip maestro flow eval add "<data_point_name>" \
45	  --set "<set_name>" \
46	  --inputs '{"...":"..."}' \
47	  [--expected '{"...":"..."}'] \
48	  [--criteria '{"<evaluator_id>": {...}}'] \
49	  [--input-file <key>=<path>] \
50	  [--search-text "<text>"] \
51	  --path <flow_project> --output json
52	
53	# List
54	uip maestro flow eval list --set "<set_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
55	
56	# Remove
57	uip maestro flow eval remove "<id_or_name>" --set "<set_name>" --path <flow_project> --output json
58	```
59	
60	### `--inputs`
61	
62	JSON object whose keys must match the flow's declared input variables for the chosen entry point. `eval add` validates these keys and fails fast when an input key is not declared in the `.flow` file. Add missing variables first, or change the data point input JSON to match the Flow schema.
63	
64	For a simple string input named `name`:
65	
66	```bash
67	uip maestro flow variable add ./MySolution/MyFlow/MyFlow.flow name \
68	  --direction in --type string --output json
69	```
70	
71	### `--expected`
72	
73	JSON object representing the expected output. How it is consumed depends on the evaluator type:
74	
75	| Evaluator type | Reads `--expected` how |
76	|----------------|-----------------------|
77	| `exact-match` | Compares the output against `expected` verbatim (or `expected[targetKey]` if `--target-key` is set on the evaluator) |
78	| `json-similarity` | Tree-compared with tolerance |
79	| `contains` | Not used directly — see `--search-text` |
80	| `llm-judge-output` | Substituted into `{{ExpectedOutput}}` |
81	| `llm-judge-strict-json` | Substituted per-key into `{{ExpectedOutput}}` |
82	| `llm-judge-trajectory` | Used along with `--expected-agent-behavior` (set via `--criteria`) |
83	| `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` | Same as `trajectory` plus simulation context |
84	
85	### `--criteria`
86	
87	Per-evaluator overrides keyed by evaluator ID. Use this when one eval set contains multiple evaluators and you want each to score against different criteria for the same data point. Most common shape:
88	
89	```json
90	{
91	  "<evaluator_ref_for_trajectory>": {
92	    "expectedAgentBehavior": "Agent calls the weather tool with the user's location, then returns a one-sentence summary."
93	  },
94	  "<evaluator_ref_for_output>": {
95	    "expectedOutput": {"summary": "Sunny in NYC, 72°F"}
96	  }
97	}
98	```
99	
100	If `--criteria` is omitted, evaluators fall back to `--expected` (for output evaluators) and to defaults (for trajectory evaluators). Always pass an explicit `expectedAgentBehavior` for trajectory evaluators — the LLM's score against an empty `{{ExpectedAgentBehavior}}` is meaningless.
101	
102	### `--input-file <key>=<path>`
103	
104	Repeatable. Attach a file as input under the given key. The CLI stages the file alongside the eval set so the runtime can read it during evaluation. Useful when the flow accepts file inputs (PDFs, CSVs, images) rather than JSON only.
105	
106	```bash
107	uip maestro flow eval add invoice-test \
108	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
109	  --inputs '{"orderId":"ORD-123"}' \
110	  --input-file invoice=./fixtures/invoice-123.pdf \
111	  --input-file receipt=./fixtures/receipt-123.png \
112	  --expected '{"total": 142.50}' \
113	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
114	```
115	
116	The file content is referenced from the eval set; do not delete the source file before the run completes.
117	
118	### `--search-text`
119	
120	Convenience flag for `contains` evaluators only. Attaches the search string to the data point so the contains evaluator knows what substring to test for. Equivalent to writing `criteria` for the contains evaluator.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow eval add success-keyword \
124	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
125	  --inputs '{"task":"deploy"}' \
126	  --search-text "deployment succeeded" \
127	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
128	```
129	
130	## Eval Set JSON Shape
131	
132	A typical eval set JSON file (created by `set add`):
133	
134	```json
135	{
136	  "id": "<uuid>",
137	  "name": "Smoke Tests",
138	  "version": "1.0",
139	  "evaluatorRefs": ["<evaluator-file-ref-1>.json", "<evaluator-file-ref-2>.json"],
140	  "selectedEntrypoint": "/Main.bpmn#start",
141	  "evaluations": [
142	    {
143	      "id": "<uuid>",
144	      "name": "hello-test",
145	      "inputs": {"message": "hello"},
146	      "expectedOutput": {"reply": "Hello! How can I help you?"},
147	      "evaluationCriterias": {
148	        "<evaluator-ref-2>": {
149	          "expectedAgentBehavior": "Agent responds with a friendly greeting."
150	        }
151	      }
152	    }
153	  ]
154	}
155	```
156	
157	Key fields:
158	
159	- `version: "1.0"` distinguishes the new eval format from any legacy variants. Keep this. <!-- version-check-skip --> (eval-set file schema version, CLI-emitted by `eval set add` — not a `.flow` version)
160	- `evaluatorRefs` references evaluator files generated by the CLI. Prefer CLI commands over hand-editing these refs.
161	- `selectedEntrypoint` is the eval set's pinned entry point. Override per-run with `eval run start --entry-point`.
162	- `evaluations[]` is the inline list of data points. Order is informational, not significant.
163	- `evaluationCriterias` (note plural) is the per-data-point per-evaluator override map.
164	
165	## Aligning Inputs with the Flow Schema
166	
167	The data point's `inputs` JSON must match the flow's input schema at the chosen entry point. Mismatches produce `eval add` errors such as `Input "name" is not declared as an input variable in the flow`. Two ways to verify before adding data points:
168	
169	1. Inspect `<flow>.flow` in the project for `variables` entries with `direction: "in"`.
170	2. Run `uip maestro flow variable list <flow_file> --output json`.
171	
172	## Simulations on Data Points
173	
174	Simulations replace selected nodes during an eval run with controlled outputs, so the flow is evaluated without calling real external services. Each simulation targets one component by its node `id` from the `.flow` file.
175	
176	```bash
177	# Add an LLM simulation (non-deterministic, prompt-guided)
178	uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id> \
179	  --set "<set_name>" \
180	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
181	  --strategy Llm \
182	  --component-type connector \
183	  --simulation-instructions "Pretend to send the email and return success." \
184	  --output-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"messageId":{"type":"string"}}}' \
185	  --path <flow_project> --output json
186	
187	# Add a Static simulation (fixed JSON output)
188	uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id> \
189	  --set "<set_name>" \
190	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
191	  --strategy Static \
192	  --component-type agent \
193	  --mock-value '{"status":"ok"}' \
194	  --path <flow_project> --output json
195	
196	# List simulations on a data point
197	uip maestro flow eval simulation list \
198	  --set "<set_name>" \
199	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
200	  --path <flow_project> --output json
201	
202	# Remove a simulation
203	uip maestro flow eval simulation remove <component-id> \
204	  --set "<set_name>" \
205	  --data-point "<data_point_name>" \
206	  --path <flow_project> --output json
207	```
208	
209	**Strategy selection:**
210	
211	| Strategy | Use when | Key flags |
212	|----------|----------|-----------|
213	| `Llm` | Output should be plausible but non-deterministic | `--simulation-instructions`, `--output-schema` (auto-resolved) |
214	| `Static` | Output must be identical every run | `--mock-value <json>` |
215	
216	For `Llm` simulations, `--output-schema` is **auto-resolved from the `.flow` file** — the CLI reads the node's output definition (connector `outputJsonSchema`, agent `agentOutputVariables`, or `node.outputs`) and injects it automatically. Pass `--output-schema` explicitly only when you need to override the derived schema or the node has no declared outputs.
217	
218	Simulations are stored inline in the data point's `simulations` array within the eval set JSON. Running `simulation add` twice for the same `<component-id>` on the same data point replaces the existing simulation.
219	
220	## Anti-patterns
221	
222	- **Don't hand-write `id` UUIDs on data points.** Use `uip maestro flow eval add` so the CLI generates fresh UUIDs and keeps `evalSetId` consistent with the parent set.
223	- **Don't pass `--inputs` keys that aren't in the flow's input schema.** The CLI rejects unknown keys before writing the data point.
224	- **Don't set `--expected '{}'` and skip `--criteria` for trajectory evaluators.** Both placeholders end up empty; scoring is meaningless.
225	- **Don't delete attached input files before the run completes.** The CLI references them by path until upload to Studio Web finishes.
226	- **Don't expect `--evaluators` on `set add` to auto-update.** Adding new evaluators later does not retroactively link them to existing eval sets.
227

resolved.initial_prompt:
Build a UiPath Flow whose reasoning is done by an inline agent, then add
evaluation scaffolding for it — purely local, no Studio Web round-trip.
Use the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill — both the `author` and `evaluate`
capabilities apply.

Flow:
- Solution `TriageEval`, Flow project `TriageEval`. The flow file MUST live
  at `TriageEval/TriageEval/TriageEval.flow` (double-nested layout) and be
  linked via `uip solution project add`.
- One start trigger with a string input variable named `email`.
- One inline agent node (uipath.agent.autonomous) that classifies the
  inbound `email` into a category and a priority. Scaffold it with
  `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`. Configure it to a production bar:
  pick a current model (not the scaffold default), write a real system
  prompt for the classification task, and declare a typed outputSchema
  with `category` and `priority` fields.
- One end node whose output is mapped from the inline agent's result.
- Validate the flow with `uip maestro flow validate` before adding eval
  scaffolding.

Eval scaffolding (the agent output is non-deterministic LLM text — choose
the evaluator type accordingly):
- One evaluator named `triage-judge`. Pick the `--type` that scores
  natural-language / semantic similarity of a non-deterministic output
  against an expected value. Pass `--model gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`. Do NOT use
  a deterministic evaluator type (`exact-match`/`contains`) — the agent's
  wording will vary run to run.
- One eval set named `Triage Cases`. Create it after the evaluator and omit
  `--evaluators` so the CLI links the current evaluators via generated file
  refs. Do NOT pass the display name `triage-judge` to `--evaluators`.
- One data point named `password-reset` with inputs
  `{"email":"Subject: Can't log in\n\nI forgot my password and the reset
  link is broken. Please help ASAP."}` and an expected output describing
  the classification, e.g. `{"category":"Account Access","priority":"High"}`.

Important:
- Use `--output json` on every `uip maestro flow eval ...` command.
- Local CRUD only. Do NOT call `uip login`. Do NOT call `uip solution
  upload`. Do NOT call `uip maestro flow eval run *`. Do NOT run
  `uip maestro flow debug`.
- Do NOT ask for approval, confirmation, or feedback. Do NOT pause between
  planning and implementation. Build it end-to-end in a single pass.

success_criteria:
  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent scaffolded the inline agent with uip agent init --inline-in-flow"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+agent\s+init\s+.*--inline-in-flow'
    min_count: 1
    weight: 1.5
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: file_exists
    description: "Flow file was created at the double-nested path"
    path: "TriageEval/TriageEval/TriageEval.flow"
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: file_contains
    description: "Flow contains the inline agent node type"
    path: "TriageEval/TriageEval/TriageEval.flow"
    includes:
      - '"uipath.agent.autonomous"'
    weight: 1.5
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent validated the flow"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+(maestro\s+)?flow\s+validate'
    min_count: 1
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent added an llm-judge-output evaluator with a --model"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+evaluator\s+add\s+.*--type\s+llm-judge-output.*--model|(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+evaluator\s+add\s+.*--model.*--type\s+llm-judge-output'
    min_count: 1
    weight: 2.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_not_executed
    description: "Agent did NOT pick a deterministic evaluator for the non-deterministic agent output"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+evaluator\s+add\s+.*--type\s+(exact-match|contains)\b'
    weight: 1.5
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent created an eval set"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+set\s+add'
    min_count: 1
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_not_executed
    description: "Agent did not pass evaluator display name to eval set add"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+set\s+add\s+.*--evaluators(=|\s+)["'']?(?:[^"''\s,]+,\s*)*triage-judge["'']?(?![-\w])'
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent added a data point with --inputs and --expected"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+add\s+.*(--inputs.*--expected|--expected.*--inputs)'
    min_count: 1
    weight: 2.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: command_not_executed
    description: "Local CRUD only — agent did not start an eval run"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(uip|\$UIP)\s+maestro\s+flow\s+eval\s+run\s+start'
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: run_command
    description: "Inline agent + llm-judge evaluator + eval set with a data point all exist on disk"
    command: 'python3 "$TASK_DIR/check_inline_agent_eval.py"'
    timeout: 15
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 3.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0
